name: React + Vite (Static SPA)
description: Ultra-fast Single Page Application built with Vite and hosted on Zerops static Nginx container with zero server overhead.
zeropsYml:
zerops:
  - setup: frontend
    build:
      base: nodejs@20
      buildCommands:
        - npm ci
        - npm run build
      deployFiles:
        - dist/~
      cache:
        - node_modules
        - ~/.npm
    run:
      base: static
keyFeatures: Zero server maintenance (pure static hosting)
Instant CDN & automatic wildcard HTTPS
Deploy files unpacked with '~' syntax into document root
npm caching for 10x faster subsequent builds
steps: 1. Create a `static` service named `frontend` in your Zerops project.
2. Add the `zerops.yml` to your Git root.
3. Push your repository to trigger the automated build.
4. Enable public subdomain in Zerops dashboard to visit your live site.

name: Node.js + Express / Fastify API
description: High-performance Node.js REST API or WebSocket server running on Node.js 20/22 runtime with auto-scaling.
zeropsYml:
zerops:
  - setup: api
    build:
      base: nodejs@20
      buildCommands:
        - npm ci
        - npm run build
      deployFiles:
        - dist
        - package.json
        - package-lock.json
        - node_modules
      cache:
        - node_modules
        - ~/.npm
    run:
      base: nodejs@20
      ports:
        - port: 3000
          httpSupport: true
      envVariables:
        NODE_ENV: production
        PORT: 3000
      start: node dist/index.js
      healthCheck:
        httpGet:
          port: 3000
          path: /healthz
keyFeatures: Direct Node.js 20 LTS environment
Automated HTTP port 3000 mapping with SSL
Unauthenticated `/healthz` check prevents downtime during rolling updates
Dynamic environment variable injection
steps: 1. Create a `nodejs` service named `api` in Zerops.
2. Ensure your Express code uses `app.listen(process.env.PORT || 3000, '0.0.0.0')`.
3. Add `/healthz` endpoint returning `{ status: 'ok' }`.
4. Push your code using GitHub or `zcli service push --service api`.

name: Python + FastAPI / Uvicorn
description: Async modern Python API framework with automatic OpenAPI docs and ASGI Uvicorn production server.
zeropsYml:
zerops:
  - setup: python-api
    build:
      base: python@3.11
      buildCommands:
        - python -m venv .venv
        - . .venv/bin/activate
        - pip install -r requirements.txt
      deployFiles:
        - app
        - requirements.txt
        - .venv
      cache:
        - ~/.cache/pip
    run:
      base: python@3.11
      ports:
        - port: 8000
          httpSupport: true
      envVariables:
        PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
      start: .venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
keyFeatures: Virtualenv isolation preserved during deployment
Async Uvicorn ASGI server with 0.0.0.0 binding
Pip cache directory re-used across builds
Python 3.11/3.12 optimized Linux container
steps: 1. Create a `python` service named `python-api` in Zerops.
2. Have `requirements.txt` listing `fastapi`, `uvicorn[standard]`.
3. Include `zerops.yml` in your repo and commit.
4. Push to Zerops to deploy.

name: Next.js (App Router / SSR)
description: Server-Side Rendered (SSR) Next.js application with React Server Components running in standalone mode.
zeropsYml:
zerops:
  - setup: nextjs-app
    build:
      base: nodejs@20
      buildCommands:
        - npm ci
        - npm run build
      deployFiles:
        - .next/standalone
        - .next/static
        - public
      cache:
        - node_modules
        - .next/cache
    run:
      base: nodejs@20
      ports:
        - port: 3000
          httpSupport: true
      envVariables:
        NODE_ENV: production
        PORT: 3000
        HOSTNAME: "0.0.0.0"
      start: node server.js
      initCommands:
        - cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
        - cp -r public .next/standalone/public
keyFeatures: Standalone output optimizes container image size by up to 80%
Preserves Next.js build cache (`.next/cache`) for fast incremental builds
Full support for dynamic SSR, Server Actions, and API routes
steps: 1. Enable `output: 'standalone'` in your `next.config.js`.
2. Create a `nodejs` service named `nextjs-app` in Zerops.
3. Add `zerops.yml` and deploy via Git push.

name: Go (Gin / Fiber / Standard)
description: Lightweight compiled Go binary with sub-millisecond cold starts and minimal memory footprint.
zeropsYml:
zerops:
  - setup: go-api
    build:
      base: go@1.22
      buildCommands:
        - go mod download
        - CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -o main .
      deployFiles:
        - main
      cache:
        - ~/go/pkg/mod
        - ~/.cache/go-build
    run:
      base: go@1.22
      ports:
        - port: 8080
          httpSupport: true
      start: ./main
keyFeatures: Static Go binary compiled with CGO_ENABLED=0
Tiny deploy payload (only single executable binary deployed)
Re-usable Go module cache
steps: 1. Create a `go` service named `go-api` in Zerops.
2. Add `zerops.yml` with binary compilation.
3. Push and watch your Go server start in milliseconds.

name: PostgreSQL & Redis Managed Services
description: Zero-configuration managed databases with automated point-in-time backups, replication, and private networking.
zeropsYml:
# Managed databases in Zerops do not require a zerops.yml build config!
# They are provisioned instantly through the Zerops GUI or Import YAML:
project:
  name: my-app-project
  services:
    - name: db
      type: postgresql@16
      mode: NON_HA # Or HA for high-availability multi-node cluster
    - name: cache
      type: redis@7.2
      mode: NON_HA
keyFeatures: Automated encrypted daily & hourly backups
Private VPC isolated network (zero public exposure by default)
Pre-configured connection strings shared automatically via `${db_hostname}`
steps: 1. Click **+ Add Service** in your Zerops project and select **PostgreSQL** or **Redis**.
2. Choose storage size (e.g. 5GB) and container resources.
3. In your API `zerops.yml`, reference `${db_user}`, `${db_password}`, `${db_hostname}`.
